tagline: From a reconstructed fort to lake chains and the Hudson.
intro: The Central Adirondack Trail makes an arc between Rome and Glens Falls through the center of Adirondack Park. Its scenery shifts from the Fulton Chain of Lakes to mountain communities and the Hudson River corridor, with a mountain-framed view of southern Lake George. New York’s scenic-byway program identifies scenic, recreational, natural and historic qualities, highlighting hamlets, regional museums and opportunities for canoeing, camping and skiing.

Waterways also carried travelers across this region: the Eckford Chain connected Blue Mountain Lake with Raquette Lake by way of the Marion River, with an onward route through the Fulton Chain to Old Forge. John Francis Brown built a 25-mile wagon trail from Remsen, but the land proved unsuitable for farming and the settlement attempt was abandoned by 1803. A railroad followed in 1888, with a station at nearby Thendara. Old Forge’s business district now serves tourism, especially in summer.

Start in Rome at the reconstructed Fort Stanwix, then head toward Old Forge and the Fulton Chain. Continue through Inlet to Raquette Lake and Blue Mountain Lake, then turn through Indian Lake toward the Hudson. The southern stretch brings you through Warrensburg on Route 9, past Lake George and into Glens Falls above the river.

moments.title: Fort Stanwix
moments.text: The fort in Rome is a National Park Service reconstruction on the site of the eighteenth-century stronghold. The original guarded the Oneida Carry, an overland connection between waterways leading toward Lake Ontario and the Hudson River. American defenders resisted a British-led siege in August 1777, contributing to the British defeat in the Saratoga campaign. In the 1960s, Rome’s leaders campaigned to reconstruct the fort as part of an urban renewal program for downtown. The present structure conceals reinforced concrete beneath earth and timber. One of the three short trails encircling it follows part of the Oneida Carry.

moments.title: Inlet
moments.text: Inlet takes its name from the eastern end of Fourth Lake, where the hamlet stands on Route 28. Fourth Lake is the largest of the eight Fulton Chain lakes, with both privately owned shoreline and state forest preserve. The community developed to serve sportsmen after the middle of the nineteenth century. Arrowhead Park occupies the site of the former Arrowhead Hotel. Chester Gillette was arrested at that hotel three days after Grace Brown’s murder at Big Moose Lake in 1906. Theodore Dreiser based An American Tragedy on the murder and included a scene at Arrowhead.

moments.title: Warrensburg
moments.text: Before it became a town, Warrensburg was known as The Bridge for its crossing of the Schroon River. That river meets the Hudson at the town’s western boundary. The local paper mill had already been partly destroyed by fire in July 1974, two years before the flood. In April 1976, spring flooding surrounded the paper mill and closed Route 418 and a nearby bridge. Workers dug a ditch under state environmental officials’ direction to relieve upstream flooding. The work caused serious erosion; the following spring, silt washed onto two downstream ranches.
